Dichotomous keys are essential tools in taxonomy. They consist of a series of statements, each highlight-
ing a distinct morphological characteristic that may be true or false depending on the organism under
observation. As the organism is compared with these statements, the key systematically directs the user
through a decision tree, ultimately leading to a specific taxonomic classification (Figure 1).
Figure 1. Dichotomous tree model with three levels; T - true, F - false.
To determine the species of an unknown organism, referred to as X, you utilize a hypothetical dichoto-
mous key with 10 levels, structurally similar to the one depicted in Figure 1. The final level of this tree
provides a conclusive taxonomic identification, with no further branching points. The tree has a complete
set of nodes without terminating branches before the final level.
A. Determining the species of an organism with more complex morphological
structures than that of organism X using the provided key will take more than
9 steps.
B. The maximal number of species that could be identified with the key is 512.
C. An identification step at level 3 (counting from the top) has four times more
possible final taxonomic outcomes than an identification step at level 5.
D. Consider three taxa A, B, and C. If A and B share a more recent common
ancestor than A and C, then the paths along the dichotomous key leading to A
and B will certainly diverge at an earlier step than the paths leading to A and C.

53BP1 protein level remains relatively same throughout the cell cycle in both normal and BRCA1 deficient

a synthetic gene-expression complex that only allows the expression of gene of interest (GOI)-encoded
protein only from the full-length mRNAs. It is composed of two parts: a toehold switch containing a

switch. When the toehold switch portion of the synthetic cassette is free, it forms a hairpin-like structure

DNA fiber assay is used to study various aspects of DNA synthesis, such as replication speed, replication
origin firing, and replication termination. It utilizes modified nucleotides to visualize the progression
of DNA replication directly. In this assay, cellular DNA is sequentially labeled with chloro-deoxyuridine
(CldU) followed by iodo-deoxyuridine (IdU), each for an equal period. Upon replication, cells incorporate
these modified nucleotides into newly synthesized DNA. Next, cells are lysed and individual DNA fibers
are stretched on a microscopic slide, followed by CldU (red) and IdU (blue) antibody staining. Finally,
DNA fibers are visualized by fluorescent microscopy.
Figure 1. Panels A-F represent replicated DNA segments. Each panel shows a single unin-
terrupted DNA molecule labeled with CldU (red) followed by IdU (blue). The white bar at the
bottom right of each panel is a scale bar of 10 μm. The DNA in all panels is from the same
organism.
A. Panel A can represent replication progression from a single replication fork,
while panel B shows replication progression from two forks.
B. Both panels C and E demonstrate replication termination.
C. In panel B, CldU is incorporated into either a leading or lagging strand of DNA
but not into both.
D. The DNA belongs to a bacterial species.
